2014_060_030414mtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education met in regular session at 7:00 PM on March 4, 2014 at Athens High School, taking up Spirit of Diversity Award recognitions, a six-item consent agenda, personnel and curriculum items, two business awards, and a closed session on negotiations. The consent agenda carried the January 2014 Treasurer's Report, which records total disbursements in the period of $4,620,849.54, of which $2,685,062.51 was check disbursements. Action items included a three-year container refuse contract to Rizzo Environmental Services at $1.48 per cubic yard, E-Rate vendor awards, an $88,555.00 special-education bus purchase from Hoekstra Transportation, and a one-time off-schedule payment of four percent for non-represented employees.
2014_060_030414mtg.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 7:00 PM, March 4, 2014, Athens High School, 4333 John R., Troy, MI 48085. District offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us); meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition**
Eleven Spirit of Diversity Award recipients, in the program's second year under the Troy Diversity & Inclusion Council: the Troy Union Giving Tree organizers (Ruba Alexander, Nancy Hanoosh, Sue Younan), the Baker Buddy Program, Joe DeVault and the Boulan Park LINKS program, Lori Medina-Yashinski and Neil Yashinski of Leonard Cultural Connections, Morse Elementary principal Stephanie Miller, and the Troy Social Justice Project team. Honorable mentions went to Tracey Kania and Duane Losey, Troy Union teachers and staff, the Oakland ISD Social Justice Project and Dr. Jay Marks, and Jen Hilzinger. Troy Youth Assistance representative Elliot Gold presented the "Dollars for Education" raffle.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the February 4 regular meeting, the February 11 workshop, the February 11 special meeting, and the February 18 special workshop; the container refuse collection award; and the January 2014 Treasurer's Report.

**Container Refuse Collection Service (Bid Package 9772)**
Kenneth D. Miller, Executive Director of Facility Operations & Purchasing, recommended Rizzo Environmental Services for 2014-2015, 2015-2016 and 2016-2017 at $1.48 per cubic yard for both trash and recycling. Current-year estimated expense from Allied Waste was $77,000.00 at 2013-2014 prices of $1.74 per cubic yard for trash and $1.66 for recycling.

January year-to-date budget reports: General Fund (101, 120, 122) revenue budget $132,247,089 against actual 58,502,071, expenditure budget $131,831,299 against actual 64,996,058, excess revenue over expenditures 415,790, and fund balance of 22,070,236 at January 1, 2014 rising to $22,486,026 at June 30, 2014. Consolidated Special Revenue Funds show a $8,832,627 revenue budget and $8,349,809 expenditure budget with a June 30, 2014 balance of $3,099,775. Debt Service Funds report $16,149,734 in budgeted revenue, 12,249,354 in property taxes collected, and a January 1 balance of (2,938,785) moving to $923,037.

**Personnel, Curriculum, Business**
Negotiations update by Assistant Superintendent Jasen Witt (report only). Probationary contract for Stacey Newcomb, .6 FTE Social Worker at Barnard and Bemis. One-time, off-schedule payment of four percent of 2012/2013 base wages for non-represented employees except the Superintendent, with base salaries frozen and no step advancement for 2013/2014. Bemis and Schroeder closed to open enrollment for 2014/2015; Athens and Troy High closed except for not more than 25 incoming ninth graders from the Troy High attendance area, application window March 5-21, 2014. E-Rate awards to Windstream ($4,361.40), Blackboard/Edline ($30,853.16), AT&T ($0.0245/minute) and Sprint ($49.99/month). Special-education bus from Hoekstra Transportation (Thomas) at $88,555.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

**Identification.** Packet 2014_060_030414mtg, titled 030414Mtg, for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of March 4, 2014 at 7:00 PM at Athens High School, 4333 John R., Troy, MI 48085. Administrative offices are at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us); meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition.** Eleven groups or individuals received Spirit of Diversity Awards in the program's second year, designed by the Troy Diversity & Inclusion Council: Ruba Alexander, Nancy Hanoosh and Sue Younan for the Giving Tree at Troy Union; the Baker Buddy Program; Joe DeVault and the Boulan Park Middle School LINKS program serving Autism Spectrum Program students; Lori Medina-Yashinski and Neil Yashinski of Leonard Cultural Connections; Morse Elementary principal Stephanie Miller; and Jesse Allgeier, Deb Sheldon, Hannah Nagi and Renee Jamil of the Troy Social Justice Project, whose students attend four Youth Leadership Summits. Honorable mentions went to Tracey Kania and Duane Losey, Troy Union teachers and staff, the Oakland ISD Social Justice Project and Dr. Jay Marks, and Jen Hilzinger. Troy Youth Assistance representative Elliot Gold announced the "Dollars for Education" raffle.

**February 4, 2014 minutes.** Secretary Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. at Troy High School with Schmidt, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff and Underwood present, President Philippart and Vice President Miletti absent, and approximately 175 audience members; adjournment was at 8:49 p.m. Senior Scholar Athletes who maintained a 3.5 cumulative grade point average were recognized, along with fall All-State athletes. Resolution 14-015 named February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy (Yes 5, No 0). Enviro-Clean Maintenance Services representatives John Thompson and Craig Wyse donated a $5,000 check to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, accepted by president Al Robinson. Resolution 14-016 approved the consent agenda including the December 2013 Treasurer's Report; Resolution 14-017 approved new hire Danielle Andresen; Resolution 14-018 certified compliance with at least 7 of 8 best-practice criteria under Section 22f of the State School Aid Act (MCL 388.1622f) for the $52 per pupil one-time incentive, citing subsections 22f(1)(a), (b), (c), (e), (f), (g) and (h) and Sections 105/105c (MCL 388.1705), adopted by roll call with all five present members voting yes; Resolution 14-019 awarded a school bus bid to Hoekstra Transportation (Thomas) for $1,659,011.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. Mr. Witt reported Fact Finding for February 26-28, and enrollment projections prepared by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants were presented at low, most likely and high levels. Other comments covered the 2013 Bond projects, the superintendent search with the Michigan Association of School Boards, TYA raffle tickets at $25 each, and closures of 4½ days districtwide with two additional days at Wattles.

**Other minutes.** The February 11 workshop (6:00 to 8:13 p.m.) covered a Technology Plan update, Network & Phone Purchase - Bond 2014, the 2013-2014 First Appropriation Act, and the 2014/15 - 2015/16 Budget Forecast. The February 11 special meeting adopted Resolution 14-020 by 7-0 roll call to enter closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), reconvening at 8:30 p.m. and adjourning at 9:49 p.m. The February 18 special workshop on the superintendent search included MASB representatives Rodney Green and Donna Oser and adjourned at 10:42 p.m.

**Container Refuse Collection Service, Bid Package 9772.** Kenneth D. Miller, Executive Director of Facility Operations & Purchasing (1140 Rankin, Troy, Michigan 48083), wrote to Mark Rajter on 20 February 2014 recommending Rizzo Environmental Services over Waste Management of Michigan and Republic Services for 2014-2015, 2015-2016 and 2016-2017. Current-year estimated expense from Allied Waste was $77,000.00, based on 2013-2014 prices of $1.74 per cubic yard for trash and $1.66 for recycling. Rizzo bid $1.48 per cubic yard for both trash and recycling in all three years, against Republic at $1.57 and Waste Management at $1.62 for 2014-2015 refuse. Estimated annual cost from Rizzo: Elementary Schools $20,317.00, Middle Schools $18,163.00, High Schools $24,935.00, Support Facilities $5,995.00, total $69,410.00. Capital Waste, CMS LLC, Griffin Disposal, Allied Waste Services and Veolia Environmental Services did not respond.

**Treasurer's Report, January 2014.** Submitted by Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, certified February 19, 2014. Check disbursements by fund: General Fund (101) 2,326,402.06; Grant Fund (120) 1,306.64; Special Education Fund (122) 142,609.35; Food Service Fund (520) 14,647.18; Troy Career Center (529) 18,016.78; Community Education Fund (530) 29,196.86; and Student Activity Fund (700, 701) 152,883.64. Totals: General Fund $2,470,318.05, Special Revenue Funds $61,860.82, Other Funds $152,883.64, total check disbursements $2,685,062.51, ACH debits $45,906.84, outgoing wire transfers $1,858,974.91, P-Card purchases $116,715.93, prior period void disbursements ($85,810.65), and total disbursements in period $4,620,849.54. The ACH and P-Card listing prints a total of $162,622.77.

Excess revenue over expenditures 415,790; fund balance 22,070,236 at January 1, 2014 and $22,486,026 at June 30, 2014. Consolidated Special Revenue Funds (520, 529, 530, 535): revenue $8,832,627 against 4,214,350; expenditures $8,349,809 against 3,311,072; excess 482,818; balance 2,616,957 to $3,099,775. Food Service (520): revenue $3,501,406 against 1,764,083; expenditures $3,415,618 against 1,195,571; excess 85,788; balance 1,098,915 to $1,184,703. Troy Career Center (529): revenue and expenditure budgets both $2,783,481, actual revenue 596,271 and expenditures 1,055,602, excess 0, fund balance $0. Adult & Community Education (530): revenue $2,366,000 against 1,788,542; expenditures $2,008,970 against 1,042,072; excess 357,030; balance 1,390,063 to $1,747,093. Facilities Rental (535): revenue $181,740 against 65,454; expenditures $141,740 against 17,827; excess 40,000; balance 127,979 to $167,979. Debt Service Funds (304, 306, 307, 312): property taxes 16,145,934 budgeted against 12,249,354 collected, total revenue $16,149,734 against 12,250,129; expenditures $12,287,912 against 1,675,198, with redemption of principal 8,660,000 untouched and interest on debt 3,324,912 against 1,662,456; excess 3,861,822; balance (2,938,785) at January 1, 2014 and $923,037 at June 30, 2014. **Wire transfers and check register.** The January wire listing totals $1,858,974.91, including payroll tax wires of $737,403.93 and $787,949.97, payroll transfers of $1,640,815.70 and $1,597,952.74, a $2,000,000.00 MILAF-to-BOA bank transfer, and MPSERS remittances of $873,507.70, $864,222.60, $837,964.04 and a $311,012.39 UAAL payment. The Pentamation ACCTPA21 check register (report date 02/05/2014, accounting period 8/14, cash accounts A1001 through A1005, check dates 01/01/2014 through 01/31/2014) prints a total report of 2,685,062.51, with the Student Activity Fund split 152,393.39 in Fund 700 and 490.25 in Fund 701. Largest items include the Michigan Education Special Services Association February 2014 billing of 933,322.55, Enviro Clean Services at 255,131.08, Blue Cross Blue Shield February 2014 premiums of 155,460.18, First Group America at 122,949.74 in the General Fund and 111,359.88 in Special Education, Bloomfield Hills Schools IB exam fees of 78,507.00, CDW Government at 75,318.17, Direct Energy at 62,603.20, Integrys Energy Services December billing of 59,934.37, Graduation Alliance at 59,640.00, and Safe Ed LLC security checks of 24,225.00 and 23,865.00; Thrun Law Firm PC received a 1,600.00 annual retainer.

**Personnel.** Item 6.A was a negotiations update by Mr. Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources, with no action required. Item 6.B recommended a probationary contract for the remainder of the 2013-2014 school year for Stacey Newcomb, .6 FTE Social Worker at Barnard and Bemis Elementary Schools, whose biographical sketch lists a B.A. in Psychology from Oakland University (April 2010), an M.A. in Social Work from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor (April 2012), a Michigan Masters Social Worker Ltd License (June 2012), and prior service at Warren Consolidated Schools and Oakland Family Services in Pontiac; she resides in Clinton Township, Michigan. Item 6.C approved a one-time, off-schedule payment for non-represented employees regularly employed during 2012/2013, excepting the Superintendent, of four percent (4%) of base wages earned July 1, 2012 through June 30, 2013, consistent with the collective bargaining agreements with the Troy Educational Secretaries Association and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association; base salaries remain frozen for 2013/2014 and no step advancement will be provided.

**Curriculum.** Bemis and Schroeder Elementary Schools were recommended closed to open enrollment for 2014/2015 because of total student enrollment and physical space constraints. Athens High and Troy High, closed for several years, were recommended closed except for not more than 25 incoming ninth grade students residing in the Troy High attendance area who wish to attend Athens, with an application window of March 5 through March 21, 2014; students with siblings attending Athens in grades 9-11 may also open enroll.

**Business.** The E-Rate/USF submission, analyzed by consultant Convergent Technology of Flint, Michigan and reviewed by Director of Technology Mark Washington in a February 27, 2014 memorandum to Dr. Fowler, recommended Windstream for Primary Rate Interface phone lines at $4,361.40 annually, though not the low bidder, because moving lines would cost at least $1500 in fees and labor; Blackboard - formerly Edline - for web hosting at $30,853.16 annually as the second highest bidder, since changing the grading system and district websites would be prohibitive; AT&T for long distance at $0.0245 per minute as the only respondent; and Sprint smartphone service from the state bid at $49.99 per month, noting Verizon is lower by $1.92 per line per month but Sprint early termination fees would exceed the savings. Amounts were to be approved as expenditures of the 2014-2015 General Fund. The special-education bus item noted a 63-passenger wheelchair-lift bus at end of life and awarded a 61-passenger bus with lift to Hoekstra Transportation (Thomas) for $88,555.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund, priced under the MSBO/Aggregate School Bus Purchasing Program and compared by Transportation Supervisor Dominick Asaro against Capital City (IC) and Holland (Bluebird). Quotation 275179, prepared by Steve Coulter of Hoekstra Transportation on 2/20/2014, firm for 30 days with estimated July 2014 delivery, specifies a 2015 Thomas Lift-Equipped Saf-T-Liner C2 School Bus 341TS on a B2 106 chassis with passenger capacity 60 + 1 WC and a Cummins ISB220 diesel at 220 HP, F.O.B. Troy, Michigan.

**Closed session.** Item 11.A provided for a resolution to enter closed session on negotiations as permitted in the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), with a roll call listing Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Philippart, Schmidt and Underwood, and no additional business other than adjournment.
